A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DR-Arena study. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-I are readable and matchable despite reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original six-agent tournament results, ablations, human studies, and analyses of 789 interaction rounds, including appendix diagnostics.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds cross-examiner validation on 50 sampled matches and human inter-annotator agreement.

M1.justification: The information-tree construction, task generation, rubric-based adjudication, and adaptive transitions remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1 in Appendix C. DEEP/WIDE becomes DEPTH/WIDTH in several places, but this is renaming. Gemini-3-Pro remains the main Examiner.

E1.justification: The same 30 Information Trees, topic and domain distributions in Appendix F, and depth/width research tasks are retained. The new examiner validation reuses existing tournament logs without adding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The six benchmark comparators in Table 4 remain unchanged. The new examiner comparison in v2 Table 7 adds GPT-5.2-Chat and Claude-Opus-4.6, comparing their adjudications with the original Gemini-3-Pro verdicts.

E3.justification: V2 adds a protocol that randomly samples 50 tournament matches, re-adjudicates them with two alternative examiners, and measures percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa. The existing tournament configuration, benchmark metrics, and human-study sample sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds a focused robustness check of whether adjudications depend on the Examiner model. The existing tree, rubric, and round-truncation ablations, as well as the appendix failure cases and distribution analyses, are retained.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports human-human verdict agreement using Cohen's kappa, adding annotation-reliability information beyond the existing human-Examiner agreement. Neither version reports confidence intervals or repeated-run uncertainty for the main leaderboard results.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports agreement/kappa of 93.02%/0.901 for GPT-5.2-Chat and 88.70%/0.839 for Claude-Opus-4.6. Table 8 adds human inter-annotator kappa of 0.88. Existing rankings, ablations, and appendix results are unchanged, including Spearman 0.94 and Pearson 0.74.

T1.justification: The graph definition, verdict categories, tournament complexity argument, and mathematical content of Algorithm 1 are retained. Terminology and subscript changes are notational; no new proofs, derivations, or formal assumptions appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of automated live-web evaluation, adaptive depth/width probing, and 0.94 correlation with human rankings. The additional validation supports these existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets cross-examiner agreement as evidence against judge-specific stylistic bias and attributes consistency to grounded rubrics. Its limitations newly acknowledge residual single-judge preferences and source-selection fairness tradeoffs. The earlier knowledge-conflict failure cases remain in Appendix G.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 now explicitly states that all pairings share the same 30 preconstructed Information Trees. V1 already describes 30 trees in total in Appendix F, so this clarifies the existing setup rather than establishing a changed experiment. Prompts, pseudocode, and repository access are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. LiveNewsBench changes from Anonymous (2025) to Zhang et al. (2026), while other references receive title, year, or publication updates; these identify existing works rather than introduce new ones.

P1.justification: V2 standardizes terminology, capitalization, punctuation, and several awkward sentences; rewrites the limitations; and adds acknowledgments. The overall section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the cross-examiner table and expands the human-audit table with an inter-annotator row. Figure 2 receives visual refinements and a spelling correction. The repository link moves to the title area, page numbers disappear, and subsequent material reflows; existing plots remain.

improvement.justification: The cross-examiner audit and human inter-annotator statistic strengthen the evidence for evaluation reliability, while the revised limitations clarify remaining judge and source-selection risks. These are useful, bounded improvements: the audit measures agreement on existing logs, and the main results and documented judge failures remain unchanged.
